quote: I used to have a $300 a month average bill, but in the last six months, it's averaging anywhere I'm paying anywhere from 600 to $1,100 a month for nothing changing.
stewart_read: This is an enormous anchor — a near-4x unexplained bill spike — and the rep validates it emotionally but never flips it into 'that's the utility robbing you' framing or ties it forward to the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be holding the flip for the closer's proposal call rather than doing it herself, which is plausible under setter_scope_discipline, but the schema still calls for at least a verbal alignment-against-utility move at capture.
coaching_implication: Coach Meg to explicitly reflect the bill number back as the villain — e.g., acknowledge the spike is the utility's fault, not his, before moving to the credit qualifier.

quote: they built a giant solar field two miles south of my house here. And ever since that went online, my electric skyrocketed.
stewart_read: Glenn is essentially building his own case for solar irony-free, unprompted — a strong engagement signal the rep could mine for rapport and curiosity.
coaching_implication: Rep should have paused and reflected: 'so a solar field helped everyone but you — let's fix that' as a light curiosity hook instead of moving straight to program mechanics.

quote: I'm a disabled vet, and I've had 31 surgeries reconstructing me over the last twenty some years.
stewart_read: Rep responds warmly and sincerely ('thank you for your service... that definitely goes far in my bliss') but does not bridge the disclosure to any solar-specific value (e.g., fixed-income stability, reliable savings for a vet).
alternative_hypothesis: The reactive read is a miss; the strategic read would require the rep to have planned a bridge in advance, which there's no evidence of — this reads as reactive warmth without a value bridge.
coaching_implication: Coach the bridge: after honoring the disclosure, tie it back — 'that's exactly why locking in a lower, predictable payment matters for guys like you.'

quote: K. I've actually I've got a a direct line that you could text me that would be better.
stewart_read: Rep offers her personal/direct line for photo transfer, which the schema flags as a privacy anti-pattern the floor currently relies on before automated capture ships.
coaching_implication: Flag for the security/privacy note in the schema; not a coaching failure specific to Meg, but worth noting as floor-wide workaround.

quote: 40 by 60. Yeah. I mean, it looks great. You've got, I mean, full sun exposure. Right? With those tree paint on it, it makes a lot a lot more possible for you, Glenn.
stewart_read: Rep is assessing roof sun exposure and making a viability call herself rather than deferring the technical read to the design team / closer.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as simple rapport-building conversation rather than technical scope creep since she doesn't discuss panel specs or savings numbers, just visually affirms what Glenn already described.
coaching_implication: Minor; keep affirmations generic ('that's great info for the design team') rather than rendering a sun-exposure verdict herself.

quote: How are you doing? I just had a a couple questions for you so we can get started on that solar design.
stewart_read: The rep never asks whether Glenn has already seen a solar design or gotten competing quotes — prior_design item was skipped entirely per verified events.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call ran long already on roof/bill logistics, the rep may have strategically dropped low-priority verify items to protect the booking — but there's no evidence she made that tradeoff deliberately.
coaching_implication: Add a quick prior_design check even on a call running long; costs 10 seconds and surfaces competitive context for the closer.
